title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 683-685): Grothendieck is identifying a group M^♮, cut out in (107) by normalisation conditions inside a group M of automorphisms. The bottom row of the diagrams is an extension 1 → 𝔊_0^+ → M → Γ̃_Q → 1, with Γ̃_Q a Galois-type quotient group. The setting is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the study of Galois/Teichmüller-type actions on profinite fundamental groups with distinguished torsion elements ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2), as in SL2(Z)^.

On the previous page he introduced two 'systems' (G; Z; L ⊂ Z; Z → Aut(G); L ↪ G). These are the data needed to build a group containing G as a normal subgroup with prescribed quotient Z/L, essentially (G ⋊ Z)/L with L embedded antidiagonally. The first system (110), built on Z_{ρ0,σ0} and L_0^♮, produces G_{ρ0,σ0}. The second (111), built on M[0] and L_0^{𝔊}, produces M. A morphism of systems, given by the identity on 𝔊_0^+, the map (108) on Z, and the inclusion of the L's, induces a morphism of the resulting groups.

This page:
(112) records the resulting morphism of extensions
1 → 𝔊_0^+ → G_{ρ0,σ0} → γ_{ρ0,σ0} → 1  over  1 → 𝔊_0^+ → M → Γ̃_Q → 1.
The quotient map γ_{ρ0,σ0} = Z_{ρ0,σ0}/L_0^♮ → Γ̃_Q = M[0]/L_0^{𝔊} is (113), induced by (108).

Since L_0^♮ is defined as the intersection Z_{ρ0,σ0} ∩ 𝔊_0^+ (i.e. Z ∩ L_0^{𝔊}), the map (113) is injective. The left vertical map is the identity, so the snake/five-lemma argument shows G_{ρ0,σ0} → M is injective. He notes in parenthesis that it is even an isomorphism under a condition like 𝔊_0^♮ ⊃ Π_0.

(114) restricts this to the subgroup 𝔊_0^♮, giving an extension 1 → 𝔊_0^♮ → G^♮_{ρ0,σ0} → γ_{ρ0,σ0} → 1 mapping into the same bottom row. One reads off that the image of G^♮_{ρ0,σ0} in M is exactly the M^♮ of (107).

The next page concludes M^♮ ≅ G^♮_{ρ0,σ0} with γ_{ρ0,σ0} ↪ Γ̃_Q. It then describes M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} as a fibre product of normalisers of ρ and σ, an extension of M^♮ by a small kernel SZ_{ρ0} × SZ_{σ0}.

Purpose: to give an intrinsic description of the normalised automorphism group M^♮ (a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like group) as an extension built from centralisers/normalisers of the torsion elements ρ, σ. That description is what lets him then compute the group M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} of automorphisms respecting both ρ and σ.
errors: No mathematical error. The injectivity argument is the standard one for a morphism of extensions with injective outer maps.
The inline remark '(c'est un iso. si 𝔊_0^♮ ⊃ Π_0 ...)' is only sketched. The precise surjectivity condition is not verified on the page.
The notation wavers between 𝔊_0^{+*} (previous page) and 𝔊_0^+ (this page) for the top-left kernel. It is the same object, since the morphism is 'l'identité sur 𝔊_0^+'.

ideas.what: Constructing a group extension from data (G, Z, Z→Aut G, L ⊂ Z with L ↪ G compatible), i.e. (G ⋊ Z)/L, and functoriality of this construction under morphisms of such data
ideas.modern_name: extension via crossed-module/pushout of semidirect product (amalgamated semidirect product)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); used by Grothendieck in SGA1-style descent of profinite extensions
ideas.where_published: related material in SGA1 Exp. IX–XIII on extensions of profinite groups; the specific formulation here is unsure

ideas.what: Injectivity of the middle map in a morphism of short exact sequences with injective outer maps, and identification of the image with the normalised subgroup M^♮
ideas.modern_name: five lemma / snake lemma for groups

ideas.what: Description of a normalised automorphism group (Galois/Teichmüller type, with ρ of order 3 and σ of order 2) as an extension of a subgroup of Γ̃_Q by 𝔊_0^♮
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on profinite π1 of M_{1,1} / SL2(Z)^ with normalisation of torsion elements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for GT̂; the Longue Marche (1981) for Grothendieck's version
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, published ed. Malgoire 1995); this specific computation is unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical bookkeeping step: a morphism of extensions, injectivity, and identification of an image. It sits inside a larger unpublished computation of Teichmüller/Galois-type groups. That context is historically interesting, but nothing on this page goes beyond standard group theory.
transcription_corrections: Top-left of (112) is 𝔊_0^+ (matching 𝔊_0^{+*} of the previous page), not a separate 𝔊_0^{~+}; the mark is a superscript +, possibly with a star or tilde.
Line '[-(1-](108), et s'identifie' should read '(108), et s'identifie :' (cross-reference to (108)).
In (113) the target is M[0]/L_0^{𝔊}; the source L appears to be L_0^♮, overwritten from another symbol.
'Par définition de L_0^♮ comme intersect[ion] Z_{ρ0,σ0} ∩ 𝔊_0^+ etc., il s'ensuit que (113) est inj., donc G_{ρ0,σ0} → M est aussi injectif'.
'On en déduit par restriction de (112) un diagramme de suites exactes' (reading confirmed).
